Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National NACOC arrests man who allegedly swallowed 58 cocaine pellets before India trip Source : Myjoyonline.com 16 November 2026 3:48pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) has arrested a 58-year-old man at the Accra International Airport after he was reportedly found to have swallowed 58 pellets suspected to contain cocaine.
The suspect was preparing to travel to India when he was identified during the Commission’s routine passenger pre-screening operations.
According to NACOC, subsequent examination revealed that he had ingested the pellets in an apparent attempt to conceal the suspected narcotic substance and transport it across international borders.
NACOC said the suspect was identified through its passenger pre-screening procedures, which are designed to detect suspicious travel patterns and possible drug trafficking activities.
The Commission said the arrest highlights the importance of intelligence-led operations, passenger profiling and airport surveillance in efforts to prevent illicit drugs from being trafficked through Ghana.
It has reiterated its commitment to strengthening surveillance and enforcement at the country's entry and exit points, with the aim of preventing Ghana from being used as a transit point for narcotics.
The Commission cautioned prospective drug traffickers against attempts to evade law enforcement by concealing or ingesting narcotic substances.
It said it would continue working with relevant national and international partners to identify and dismantle drug trafficking networks.
The arrest comes amid heightened attention on Ghana’s role in international drug trafficking following major narcotics seizures involving consignments reportedly linked to the country.
One such case involved a reported 3.9-tonne cocaine seizure at the Port of Dunkirk in France. The drugs were concealed in a consignment of plastic waste reportedly shipped from Ghana.
The incident has attracted political scrutiny, with the Minority in Parliament calling for a parliamentary inquiry into the circumstances surrounding the shipment and the country's response to drug trafficking.
The 58-year-old suspect is expected to be arraigned before court as investigations continue.
